angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 537,776 km at 201.75 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 4.9567 +/- 0.0137 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 201.75 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.773 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Kang et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.528.1930K/abstract): 537,776 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.807 +/- 0.034 solar masses from Kang et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.528.1930K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4962 +/- 39 K from Kang et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.528.1930K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kang et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-19 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.528.1930K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-19.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.569, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-19 (pscomppars): spectral type K1, from Hartman et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJ...726...52H/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HAT-P-19: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-19 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.166 dex, from Kang et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.528.1930K/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-19 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.48545, from Kang et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.528.1930K/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-19 (pscomppars): age 7.2 Gyr, from Kang et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.528.1930K/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-19 (pscomppars): rotation period 35.5 d, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-19 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.7 km/s, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.773 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.635. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
